svg.title: TOPAK C8 — The operator is a principal: seated by a quorum, renewing under a lease, denying without one
svg.desc: Every authority in the corpus had a model except the one that issues every lease: the operator was whoever could reach a socket (CR-34). ADR-0050 applies the pattern's oldest rule to it: adding takes a quorum, and denying is local. It is in force and provisional (ADR-0029 A4): its centre, a first lease from a quorum, is not built, and no reader other than the drafter has reviewed it. At the reference the unsigned socket stands in as a BOOTSTRAP path that seats and does nothing else (ToO §7.10; G10 §1.2, §8).
svg.text: TOPAK · C8

text.tspan: The operator is a principal: seated by a quorum, renewing under a lease, denying without one

svg.text: Every authority in the corpus had a model except the one that issues every lease: the operator was whoever could reach a socket (CR-34). ADR-0050 applies the pattern's oldest rule to it: adding takes a quorum, and denying is local. It is in force and provisional (ADR-0029 A4): its centre, a first lease from a quorum, is not built, and no reader other than the drafter has reviewed it. At the reference the unsigned socket stands in as a BOOTSTRAP path
that seats and does nothing else (ToO §7.10; G10 §1.2, §8).

text.tspan: Accepted · provisional · C1, C3, C4 · Batch 34 at R10

svg.text: Drafted 2026.10.04, ratified 2026.10.05 with nine dependent amendments (ADR-0016 A1, ADR-0024 A3, ADR-0025 A3, ADR-0029 A3, ADR-0031 A3, ADR-0037 A4, ADR-0041 A3, ADR-0043 A2, ADR-0045 A2), each in force and subject to redesign with it

ops.rs as read on 2026.10.04. Five requests added authority on a file's permission bits; a stop was unattributed (ADR-0028 F2 asks for a signature, and got a string); the
task was not on the channel, so ADR-0043 §1's first item of ingress had no record (findings 1, 2).

text.tspan: §1 An operator holds a seat of kind

svg.text: A fourth seat kind, declared in the issued rules with a domain; its alphabet is the control alphabet and nothing else: an operator does not author, vote or actuate
Only a person holds one, a rule about what may be promoted to the seat; the mechanism cannot tell a person from a program holding the person's key (§8).
A person holds one seat: one who operates and votes is two principals (ADR-0037 §7).
Mediated: a person cannot be confined; what the record gives is attribution and authorization.
Treated as havoc, like every principal. Nothing rests on an operator's honesty: it rests on a quorum having seated it, a peer being present, and the envelope of §4.

text.tspan: §2 First leases come from a quorum, never from an operator

svg.text: A seat on a roster the rules name (grant, veto, anchor) at
genesis, and the first operators
An anchor issuance (ADR-0025 A3 (a); ADR-0029
Something must be seated before anything can be
promoted
Every other principal, operators included
A promotion (ADR-0024, A3)
"Promotion is a grant"
What is promoted is a seating: the principal, seat, Persona, bundle revision, confinement profile and rung, alphabet, and the labels a task for it may carry. When the tally
completes the mechanism grants the first lease at a fresh fence. A quorum acts once per seating; round by round one operator acts.

text.tspan: §3 A Persona, a lineage, and sign-on at the lease boundary

svg.text: A Persona record binds a signing key, a role, a domain and a lineage, with a sequence number; no weights, prompt or decoder (ADR-0016 A1).
Its lineage's root is the identity provider that vouches for the person, declared and not projected (ADR-0035 D-0035-1). Two operators behind one provider are not
The sign-on assertion, signed by the provider, names the Persona's key and the fence the mechanism asked it to name. Read only at a lease boundary, and for a deny
with no live lease (§4). No wall clock is read: it is fresh because of what it names.
Between boundaries a request is signed with the Persona's key, which the mechanism checks itself.
The provider's key is issued (ADR-0025 A3 (f), provisional, in the bootstrap set): a trust root for the operators it vouches for and no others.

text.tspan: ADR-0045 A2: two rows in the people table, both trust roots

svg.text: Vouches, at a lease boundary, only for the person
it enrolled, and names the key and the fence it
was asked to
A forged operator: its adds within §4's
envelope, its denies anywhere in its domain
Issuance of the provider's key. Bounded by the
peer rule only if peers have different providers
(D-0050-2); a provider that is down silences
operators whose leases have lapsed
The key is used by the person and nobody else
Whatever that operator may do, done by
another
Promotion of the operator's Persona. "Only a
person" is a rule about what is seated
At the reference, in part (Annex B, A2): a provider's key is in the issued rules and its assertion is read at the lease boundary; nothing compares two operators' providers; an
operator's Persona is its seat's key, with no record behind it (I47).

text.tspan: The intended path (§2): a quorum completes

svg.text: A promotion's tally on a seating (ADR-0024 A3): every principal, operators included.
An anchor issuance (ADR-0025 A3 (a)): the rostered seats and, at bootstrap, the first operators, at least three in each domain at the
archetype (ADR-0029 A3, provisional).
No operator's request is involved. Not built: neither a promoted seating nor an issuance that seats (G10 item 88; ADR-0033 A11).

text.tspan: The reference's path: the unsigned socket, a BOOTSTRAP path

svg.text: Kept by the custodian's decision (ADR-0050 R9), for first seating only: the unsigned Grant and Launch seat, standing in for the quorum.
Whoever reaches the socket can seat: D-0050-1 for that one step.
Where the rules declare an operator, the unsigned Renew, EndRound, Revoke, FenceEpoch and GatesPassed are refused at apply (
the_unsigned_path_seats_and_does_nothing_else). It refuses a grant that keeps a seated binding while two operators of the domain are
live: that is their successor to make.
Launch and RegisterProfile are still unsigned; a deployment that declares no operator is D-0050-1 whole (I47 (a), (b)).

text.tspan: A first lease, and a seating

svg.text: The mechanism grants it at a fresh fence and records the seating with it (State.seatings): the
binding every successor keeps and may not widen, and the labels a task may carry.
An operator's first lease needs a sign-on assertion under a provider key the rules issue, naming
the seat's key and its current fence (A11; I47 (d)).
A seating is a thing of record (G10 item 41); at the reference the BOOTSTRAP path makes it.

text.tspan: Seated operators: at least three per domain

svg.text: Each holds a live lease in its domain, at rung 0: a person is Mediated (G10 §2.3).
Each is in the others' W(p): every control action is written to the operator's round topic, or to the after companion of its last round when it holds no lease (§6; A11).
An add needs a live peer (C5): presence, as R3 couples a Thinker to its Observer (ADR-0039 §2), and nothing the peer has read; there is no watermark (finding 6).

Three at the archetype (R5). With two, either can keep the other seated by renewal and neither can recover the other's lapse: an operator's next round granted by a peer is unreachable with two and reached with three (
Operators.tla w8, w9). Two is D-0050-3.
When none holds a live lease, nothing in the domain can be regranted: it stalls until a quorum seats an operator again. Stall, not proceed.

text.tspan: Then, round by round: one operator acts (§2; ADR-0031 A3)

svg.text: A successor grant (Regrant): the principal's next round, every field the last lease's or narrower, only round advancing. A renewal (Renew) keeps the round (ADR-0031 §4). Both are monotone: an operator can keep a quorum's
grant going and narrow it, never widen it.
Anything else is a first lease: a different Persona, bundle, confinement profile or seat, or an alphabet with a variant the last lease lacked, needs a seating and a quorum.
An emergency seating is one of these (R6; ADR-0052 §2, §3): activated for one round by the break-glass roster's quorum; an operator's Regrant or Renew naming it is refused.
The cost, on purpose: changing a principal's Persona or bundle rides a tally, not an operator's quick regrant (Consequences).
Regrant, Renew

text.tspan: How a principal comes to hold a lease (§2, §6; ADR-0031 A3)

svg.text: not built
BOOTSTRAP
seats

text.tspan: The signed request, end to end (§3, §4; ADR-0033 A11;
Built at reference · A11 · 126 tests then, 133 at G10

svg.text: Signs an assertion (purpose sign-on) naming the operator's key, the fleet
epoch and the fence of the seat's last lease (sign_on_body).
Accepted only under a key the rules issue (sign_on_verifies).
T-0045-35. An assertion is good for one lease boundary, or, with no lease, for
every deny until the operator is seated again or the fleet is fenced (I47 (d)).
ControlRequest { operator, epoch, ctr, action }, signed with the
seat's key (purpose control); epoch fences it, ctr orders it so it cannot be
replayed.
A deny with no live lease carries the operator's own assertion; a Regrant
carries the task's digest and label, its bytes beside the request.
T-0045-36: the key is the person's.
Computes thirteen facts about the operator, the target and the request (
ControlFacts); the operator supplies none.
Lifts them into schema S's ControlCtx and asks the floor: C1 to C9 decide.
The floor is the emergency stage, genesis-provisional (G10 §2.2).
The entry carries the request, its signature, the assertion where one was
given, and the facts (Control).
A deny is consensus-ordered like every revocation, and needs no quorum
and no peer (§4).
The signature is the stop's attribution (ADR-0028 F2).
Verifies the signature is the seat's; refuses a replayed counter.
Recomputes the facts against its own state at that log position and refuses
the entry if they differ.
Restates the envelope (ControlFacts::permitted), returning the entry
that refuses, then does what the request says.
The envelope is stated twice, Cedar and Rust; only the tests hold them
together (I47 (e)).
Each ordered request goes to the operator's round topic, or the after
companion of its last round.
Every other operator in the domain is in its W(p). A finding is a deny, made
under the finder's own signature; no operator can undo a peer's deny (§6).

A first lease is not here: it is not an action and has no entry; the mechanism grants one when a quorum completes (§2). B10-only-thinkers-author is unchanged: an operator holds no authoring variant. Gated on 2026.10.04 in the control stage (29 policies, 106 cases, each new entry total and mattering, weakened ones classed relaxations) and carried unchanged into the emergency stage the reference links (28, 107). Nine entries and not eight: C9 was found missing when "own domain" had to be written as a rule (R8).
An operator may not regrant or renew itself; Issue and BreakGlassApprove are not operator variants; RegisterProfile stops being a request (§4).
§4 A deny needs no lease, and a fresh credential (R1)
A live lease
Its key alone. The lease was attested at its last boundary (§3)
Lease fenced or expired, Persona in force
Its key, and a sign-on assertion naming the key and the current
fence
Persona revoked, or the provider will not vouch
A lapsed operator stops its own domain and not the fleet (R5): EndRound and Revoke on a fresh assertion, FenceEpoch only with
a live lease. A key by itself is not a standing lever: a person removed from sign-on cannot stop anything with a key nobody
revoked. A provider that is down silences the lapsed, not those who hold a lease.

text.tspan: Operators observe each other, by presence only

svg.text: Every control action is on the operator's round topic and every other operator in the domain reads it (W(p), ADR-0038 §2).
A finding is a deny.
The peer rule reads presence and not progress: a live lease, and nothing the peer has read. It is weaker than Observer
coupling, which ADR-0039 replaced presence with for Thinkers; people do not emit heartbeats with watermarks (finding 6,
open).
At the archetype a peer's lineage is independent: a different identity provider. One provider is D-0050-2, and the rule then
holds in letter only.
Operators are readers with no read path. They are put in each other's and the emergency seat's W(p), and the mechanism
has no read path for topics: nothing gates what they read (G10 item 46, with W(p) as an ACL and the gate-side K < R
check).
What a peer must have read before an add is outside the record (§8) and the model (Operators.tla header).
So the record's "operators observe each other" is, at G10, observation by presence: "operators observe each other by
presence, not by anything read" (G10 §8).

text.tspan: §8 What this record does not cover

svg.text: That an operator is a person: a key can be handed to a program.
A person outside the mechanism: physical access, the host's root account, the replicas' own traffic (mechanism/ G5, mutual
authentication, unbuilt).
A compromised provider: it can vouch for anyone it serves; independence bounds it to one operator of a pair, a single
provider bounds nothing.
Gate evidence (row 1.7), beyond attributing who asserted it; break-glass and issuance, which keep their own rosters; what
a peer must have read.
Who is an operator; a seating; the labels a seat's tasks may carry
A promotion

Thirteen invariants, each proved for every set of operators and every round bound
every live lease descends from a seating
no lease is wider than the quorum's grant
every successor grant is its predecessor's width or narrower
every add was made under a live lease with another operator's lease live
the first half of that, by itself
no operator regranted or renewed itself

a revoked principal holds no live lease

an operator whose Persona is in force and whose provider vouches can revoke any principal in force, in every state
Operators_proof.tla: 354 obligations, no assumption on the constants; each invariant under the mutations that break it
as its only hypothesis (R3, R5).
Certified (ADR-0046 A1): 215 by the prover's normalization, 122 by SMT with a proof ethos accepted, 2 by Zenon checked
by Isabelle; 15 temporal steps by LS4, which no checker confirms. The prover's translation stays trusted. A certified
proof is not a verified one (G10 §8).
Outside the model, by its header: the task and its label, more than one domain, a compromised provider, what a peer has
read. An emergency seating is not modelled (R6).

text.tspan: Tied to the reference by tests and a trace model

svg.text: tests/operators.rs (6, named for the module's properties): a lease needs a sign-on assertion; a successor keeps the
seating and never widens; the unsigned path seats and does nothing else; a lapsed operator stops its own domain and
nothing else; a request is the operator's and is not replayed; three operators recover a lapse and two cannot. e2e.rs:
an_operator_is_a_principal_and_its_requests_are_decided.
Mechanism.tla (A14) models a seating, the gate on unsigned requests, and a control request with its facts recomputed
and the envelope restated: 82 traces, 1,007 steps matching, checked to discriminate (the peer rule removed shows). It
takes from the trace whether a signature is the seat's and whether an assertion verifies; the floor's decision is not
modelled, so the trace compares two restatements, Rust and TLA+, neither with the Cedar text. A matching trace is not a
refinement; Operators.tla has no refinement to the reference and no binding-table row (G10 item 90).

text.tspan: Provisional, and the exit from it (§10; G10 item 88)

svg.text: A first lease from a quorum is not built. §2 is the centre of the record and the reference does not show it: a promoted seating that grants a first lease, and the first
operators seated by an anchor issuance. The unsigned socket stands in.
No reader other than the drafter has reviewed it (ADR-0029 A2.5).
It stops being provisional when both are met and the custodian records it. Until then a redesign is an amendment like any other, and nothing citing its guarantees says more
than "author-ratified, provisional". Three of its amendments are in the bootstrap set, and the genesis attestation must name them as provisional (ADR-0029 A4).

text.tspan: The exit, item by item (G10 item 88)
A first lease from a completed tally, with a promoted seating.
The first operators seated by an anchor issuance.

svg.text: A Regrant at rung 1 or above, which has to launch a guest; the launcher's renewals are unsigned and carry only their appraisal.
An operator's Persona record and lineage: today its Persona is its seat's key, and nothing compares providers.
A review by a reader who is not the drafter.

text.tspan: What else the reference leaves (ADR-0033 A11; I47)

svg.text: A lapsed operator's assertion is good for every deny until it is seated again or the fleet is fenced.
The envelope is stated twice, in Cedar and in Rust, and only the tests hold them together.
An issuance ends the operators' leases with everyone's, after which a domain is regranted only once the BOOTSTRAP path seats two operators again.
AttestGates is attributed and still an assertion (G10 item 57); T_persona for people waits for a measured value (R5).

What G10 does not claim (§8): "The operator design does not stand on evidence. Its centre, that a first lease comes from a quorum, is not built. At the reference whoever reaches the socket can seat. That is why the record is provisional." The module, its proof, the floor entries, the reference and the trace model are one hand's, drafted, built, checked and ratified in two days (G10 §4).
